prompt:
Create one full-body production illustration for a 2D fighting game: Nemesis SECOND FORM from the original Resident Evil 3: Nemesis (1999), the exact incarnation in reference image 1. Reference image 1 is the complete original body appearance source. Reference image 2 is a previously generated selection portrait and may be used ONLY for matching rendering style, material palette and detail density; it is not anatomical evidence. Keep the 1999 second-form identity, proportions, scarred stitched head with its single pale eye and exposed teeth, purple parasite tubes and their asymmetric routes, bare upper body with the exact visible shoulder/chest details, ragged dark trousers, long hands, heavy dark shoes and trailing parasite tendrils as documented by image 1. Preserve the source anatomical left and right; turn the character naturally rather than horizontally mirroring the artwork. Do not borrow the first-form trenchcoat, rocket launcher or anatomy from the 2020 remake, and do not invent new parts or decorations.

The entire fighter is present in ONE image, in one static ready-to-fight idle BASE POSE, facing SCREEN-RIGHT in a readable front/three-quarter side-view 2D fighting-game stance. Keep both feet planted in a stable, slightly staggered combat stance, knees slightly flexed and hands ready. Choose a three-quarter angle that keeps the documented front body readable. Keep every hand, finger, shoe and the complete tips of the documented trailing tentacles inside the canvas. Retain source-supported proportions and appendages; no duplicated limbs. Leave comfortable transparent padding around the entire silhouette, particularly around the shoes and long tendrils. Match the restrained realistic shaded game-asset rendering of the existing portrait, without a thick cartoon outline or glow. One isolated subject, transparent background, no floor or cast ground shadow, no labels, scenery, frame, montage or animation grid. This is one static generated base pose, not an original Capcom sprite or an animation cycle.
